name: The Duniway Hotel
insider_take: The Duniway captures Portland's rebellious spirit in the heart of downtown, where craft culture meets urban sophistication.
whats_special: Named after suffragette Abigail Scott Duniway, this boutique hotel sits in Portland's Cultural District, just steps from the iconic Pioneer Courthouse Square. The property features locally-sourced art throughout and Mayrose restaurant, which showcases the Pacific Northwest's renowned farm-to-table dining scene.
pro_tip: Book a corner room on higher floors for stunning views of the Willamette River and Mount Hood on clear days.
dont_miss: Walk two blocks to Powell's City of Books, the world's largest independent bookstore spanning an entire city block. The hotel's location also puts you within walking distance of the Portland Art Museum and the vibrant Pearl District's galleries and boutiques.
pros: Prime downtown Portland location near major attractions
Modern boutique hotel with sophisticated design
Excellent fitness center and wellness amenities
cons: Limited parking availability in downtown location
Urban setting may have street noise
